raw: CHAPTER VII. Monseigneur in Town
en: [Chapter 7] Monseigneur in Town

raw: Monseigneur, one of the great lords in power at the Court, held his fortnightly reception in his grand hotel in Paris.
en: Monseigneur, one of the most powerful lords at Court, held a reception every two weeks at his grand mansion in Paris.
ko: 궁정에서 가장 권력 있는 영주 중 한 명인 몽세뇌르는 파리의 웅장한 저택에서 2주마다 연회를 열었다.

raw: Monseigneur was in his inner room, his sanctuary of sanctuaries, the Holiest of Holiests to the crowd of worshippers in the suite of rooms without.
en: Monseigneur was in his private inner room, his holy sanctuary, while a crowd of worshippers waited in the outer rooms.
ko: 몽세뇌르는 그의 성스러운 안식처인 개인 내실에 있었고, 바깥 방들에는 숭배자들의 무리가 기다리고 있었다.

raw: Monseigneur was about to take his chocolate.
en: Monseigneur was preparing to drink his morning hot chocolate.
ko: 몽세뇌르는 아침용 핫초콜릿을 마실 준비를 하고 있었다.

raw: Monseigneur could swallow a great many things with ease, and was by some few sullen minds supposed to be rather rapidly swallowing France; but, his morning’s chocolate could not so much as get into the throat of Monseigneur, without the aid of four strong men besides the Cook.
en: Monseigneur was capable of swallowing many things with ease. A few bitter minds accused him of rapidly swallowing up the wealth of France. But his morning chocolate could not even reach his throat without the help of four strong men in addition to the cook.
ko: 몽세뇌르는 많은 것을 쉽게 삼킬 수 있는 능력이 있었다. 몇몇 비판적인 사람들은 그가 프랑스의 부를 빠르게 삼켜버린다고 비난했다. 하지만 그의 아침 초콜릿은 요리사 외에도 네 명의 건장한 사내들의 도움이 없이는 목구멍에 닿을 수조차 없었다.

raw: Yes.
en: Indeed, it took four men to get the chocolate to his lips.
ko: 실제로 초콜릿을 그의 입술에 가져다 대는 데만 네 명의 남자가 필요했다.

raw: It took four men, all four ablaze with gorgeous decoration, and the Chief of them unable to exist with fewer than two gold watches in his pocket, emulative of the noble and chaste fashion set by Monseigneur, to conduct the happy chocolate to Monseigneur’s lips.
en: All four were decorated in gold and fine clothing. Their leader required at least two gold watches in his pocket, just to copy the noble fashion set by Monseigneur.
ko: 네 명 모두 금과 훌륭한 옷으로 치장되어 있었다. 그들의 우두머리는 몽세뇌르가 정한 귀족 유행을 모방하기 위해 주머니에 최소한 두 개의 금시계가 필요했다.

raw: One lacquey carried the chocolate-pot into the sacred presence; a second, milled and frothed the chocolate with the little instrument he bore for that function; a third, presented the favoured napkin; a fourth (he of the two gold watches), poured the chocolate out.
en: One servant carried the chocolate pot; a second frothed the drink with a small whisk; a third offered a napkin; and a fourth, the one with the two gold watches, poured it out.
ko: 한 하인은 초콜릿 주전자를 날랐고, 두 번째 하인은 작은 거품기로 음료의 거품을 냈으며, 세 번째 하인은 냅킨을 제공했고, 두 개의 금시계를 찬 네 번째 하인이 그것을 따랐다.

raw: It was impossible for Monseigneur to dispense with one of these attendants on the chocolate and hold his high place under the admiring Heavens.
en: It was impossible for Monseigneur to do without any of these servants and still maintain his high social standing.
ko: 몽세뇌르가 높은 사회적 지위를 유지하면서 이 하인들 중 단 한 명이라도 없이 지내는 것은 불가능했다.

raw: Deep would have been the blot upon his escutcheon if his chocolate had been ignobly waited on by only three men; he must have died of two.
en: It would have been a terrible disgrace to his family name if his chocolate had been served by only three men; he would have died of shame if there were only two.
ko: 만약 그의 초콜릿이 단 세 명의 남자에게서 제공되었다면 그의 가문 이름에 끔찍한 불명예가 되었을 것이고, 단 두 명뿐이었다면 그는 수치심에 죽었을 것이다.

raw: Monseigneur had been out at a little supper last night, where the Comedy and the Grand Opera were charmingly represented.
en: Monseigneur had attended a private dinner party the night before, where actresses and opera singers were present.
ko: 몽세뇌르는 전날 밤 여배우들과 오페라 가수들이 참석한 사적인 만찬에 참석했었다.

raw: Monseigneur was out at a little supper most nights, with fascinating company.
en: He went out to such parties almost every night with charming company.
ko: 그는 매력적인 동반자들과 거의 매일 밤 그런 파티에 나갔다.

raw: So polite and so impressible was Monseigneur, that the Comedy and the Grand Opera had far more influence with him in the tiresome articles of state affairs and state secrets, than the needs of all France.
en: Monseigneur was so polite and easily influenced that comedies and opera singers had far more influence on him regarding state affairs and secrets than the actual needs of all France.
ko: 몽세뇌르는 너무나 정중하고 쉽게 영향을 받았기 때문에, 모든 프랑스의 실제 필요보다 코미디나 오페라 가수가 국가의 일과 비밀에 대해 그에게 훨씬 더 많은 영향을 미쳤다.

raw: A happy circumstance for France, as the like always is for all countries similarly favoured!--always was for England (by way of example), in the regretted days of the merry Stuart who sold it.
en: This was a happy circumstance for France, as such things always are for countries favored with similar rulers, just as it had been for England when the merry King Charles II sold his country to France.
ko: 쾌활한 찰스 2세가 영국을 프랑스에 팔아넘겼을 때 영국에 그랬던 것처럼, 비슷한 통치자들의 은총을 받은 국가들에 항상 그렇듯 이는 프랑스에 행복한 상황이었다.

raw: Monseigneur had one truly noble idea of general public business, which was, to let everything go on in its own way; of particular public business, Monseigneur had the other truly noble idea that it must all go his way--tend to his own power and pocket.
en: Monseigneur had one noble idea about public business in general: to let everything take care of itself. As for his own private business, he believed everything must go his way to increase his power and wealth.
ko: 몽세뇌르는 일반적인 공무에 대해 한 가지 고귀한 생각을 가지고 있었다. 즉, 모든 것이 스스로 해결되도록 내버려두는 것이었다. 자신의 사적인 사업에 관해서는 그의 권력과 부를 늘리기 위해 모든 것이 자신의 방식대로 되어야 한다고 믿었다.

raw: Of his pleasures, general and particular, Monseigneur had the other truly noble idea, that the world was made for them.
en: Regarding his pleasures, he was convinced that the world had been created solely for his enjoyment.
ko: 그의 쾌락에 관해서 그는 세상이 오로지 그의 즐거움을 위해 창조되었다고 확신했다.

raw: The text of his order (altered from the original by only a pronoun, which is not much) ran: “The earth and the fulness thereof are mine, saith Monseigneur.”
en: His motto was: "The earth and everything in it belong to me, says Monseigneur."
ko: 그의 좌우명은 "지구와 그 안의 모든 것은 내 것이다, 몽세뇌르가 말하노라."였다.

raw: Yet, Monseigneur had slowly found that vulgar embarrassments crept into his affairs, both private and public; and he had, as to both classes of affairs, allied himself perforce with a Farmer-General.
en: Yet Monseigneur had slowly realized that financial troubles were creeping into both his public and private affairs.
ko: 그러나 몽세뇌르는 자신의 공적, 사적 업무 모두에 재정적인 문제가 서서히 기어들고 있다는 것을 서서히 깨닫고 있었다.

raw: As to finances public, because Monseigneur could not make anything at all of them, and must consequently let them out to somebody who could; as to finances private, because Farmer-Generals were rich, and Monseigneur, after generations of great luxury and expense, was growing poor.
en: As for public finances, Monseigneur couldn't make any sense of them at all, so he had to rent them out to someone who could. As for his private finances, the Farmer-Generals were incredibly rich, and Monseigneur was growing poor after his family had lived in great luxury and expense for generations.
ko: 공공 재정에 관해서 몽세뇌르는 전혀 이해할 수 없었기 때문에 할 수 있는 사람에게 임대해야 했다. 그의 사적인 재정에 관해서 말하자면 농민 징세관들은 엄청나게 부유했고, 몽세뇌르는 그의 가문이 대대로 엄청난 사치와 낭비 속에서 살아온 후 점점 가난해지고 있었다.

raw: Hence Monseigneur had taken his sister from a convent, while there was yet time to ward off the impending veil, the cheapest garment she could wear, and had bestowed her as a prize upon a very rich Farmer-General, poor in family.
en: Because of this, Monseigneur had pulled his sister out of a convent just in time to stop her from taking the veil—the cheapest outfit she could possibly wear—and handed her over as a prize to a very rich Farmer-General who lacked a good family name.
ko: 이 때문에 몽세뇌르는 누이가 입을 수 있는 가장 값싼 옷인 수녀 베일을 쓰기 직전에 수녀원에서 그녀를 빼내어, 훌륭한 가문 이름이 없는 매우 부유한 농민 징세관에게 전리품처럼 넘겨주었다.

raw: Which Farmer-General, carrying an appropriate cane with a golden apple on the top of it, was now among the company in the outer rooms, much prostrated before by mankind--always excepting superior mankind of the blood of Monseigneur, who, his own wife included, looked down upon him with the loftiest contempt.
en: For his private finances, because he was growing poor after generations of luxury, he relied on the Farmer-General's wealth. Therefore, Monseigneur had taken his sister out of a convent.
ko: 그의 사적인 재정을 위해, 그는 대대로 이어진 사치 후 가난해지고 있었기 때문에 농민 징세관의 부에 의지했다. 따라서 몽세뇌르는 여동생을 수녀원에서 데리고 나왔다.

raw: A sumptuous man was the Farmer-General.
en: Letting her become a nun would have been the cheapest way to support her, but instead, he married her off to a very rich tax collector from a low-class family.
ko: 그녀를 수녀가 되게 하는 것이 그녀를 부양하는 가장 비용이 덜 드는 방법이었을 테지만, 대신 그는 그녀를 하층민 출신의 아주 부유한 세금 징수원에게 시집보냈다.

raw: Thirty horses stood in his stables, twenty-four male domestics sat in his halls, six body-women waited on his wife.
en: This tax collector, carrying a cane with a golden apple on top, was now in the outer rooms.
ko: 꼭대기에 황금 사과가 달린 지팡이를 들고 있는 이 세금 징수원이 지금 바깥 방들에 있었다.

raw: As one who pretended to do nothing but plunder and forage where he could, the Farmer-General--howsoever his matrimonial relations conduced to social morality--was at least the greatest reality among the personages who attended at the hotel of Monseigneur that day.
en: The crowd bowed low before him, except for the noble relatives of Monseigneur, who, along with his own wife, looked down on him with utter contempt.
ko: 몽세뇌르의 귀족 친척들, 그리고 심지어 자신의 아내와 함께 그를 완전한 경멸로 내려다보는 사람들을 제외하고는, 무리는 그에게 깊이 머리를 숙였다.

raw: For, the rooms, though a beautiful scene to look at, and adorned with every device of decoration that the taste and skill of the time could achieve, were, in truth, not a sound business; considered with any reference to the scarecrows in the rags and nightcaps elsewhere (and not so far off, either, but that the watching towers of Notre Dame, almost equidistant from the two extremes, could see them both), they would have been an exceedingly uncomfortable business--if that could have been anybody’s business, at the house of Monseigneur.
en: The tax collector was a very wealthy man. He kept thirty horses in his stables, twenty-four male servants in his halls, and six ladies-in-waiting for his wife. As someone whose only job was to plunder and gather wealth wherever he could, he was at least the most honest reality among the guests at Monseigneur’s mansion that day.
ko: 그 세금 징수원은 매우 부유한 남자였다. 그는 마구간에 서른 마리의 말, 홀에 스물네 명의 남자 하인, 그리고 아내를 위해 여섯 명의 시녀를 두었다. 할 수 있는 한 어디서나 약탈하고 부를 긁어모으는 것이 유일한 직업인 사람으로서, 그는 적어도 그날 몽세뇌르의 저택에 온 손님들 중에서 가장 정직한 현실이었다.

raw: Military officers destitute of military knowledge; naval officers with no idea of a ship; civil officers without a notion of affairs; brazen ecclesiastics, of the worst world worldly, with sensual eyes, loose tongues, and looser lives; all totally unfit for their several callings, all lying horribly in pretending to belong to them, but all nearly or remotely of the order of Monseigneur, and therefore foisted on all public employments from which anything was to be got; these were to be told off by the score and the score.
en: Although the rooms were beautiful and decorated with the finest art of the time, they did not represent a healthy society. Nearby lived starving people in rags and nightcaps. The towers of Notre Dame Cathedral could easily see both worlds, the mansion and the misery, standing between the two extremes.
ko: 비록 방들은 아름답고 당대 최고의 예술품들로 장식되어 있었지만, 그것들은 건강한 사회를 대변하지는 않았다. 근처에는 누더기를 입고 나이트캡을 쓴 굶주린 사람들이 살고 있었다. 노트르담 대성당의 탑들은 그 두 극단 사이에 서서 저택과 비참함이라는 두 세계를 쉽게 볼 수 있었다.

raw: People not immediately connected with Monseigneur or the State, yet equally unconnected with anything that was real, or with lives passed in travelling by any straight road to any true earthly end, were no less abundant.
en: If anyone at Monseigneur's house ever bothered to think about it, the contrast would have seemed like an uncomfortable business.
ko: 만약 몽세뇌르의 집에 있는 누군가가 그것에 대해 굳이 생각해 보았더라면, 그 대조는 불편한 일처럼 보였을 것이다.

raw: Doctors who made great fortunes out of dainty remedies for imaginary disorders that never existed, smiled upon their courtly patients in the ante-chambers of Monseigneur.
en: The guests included military officers with no knowledge of war, naval officers who knew nothing of ships, civil servants with no idea how to govern, and hypocritical priests with greedy eyes and loose morals.
ko: 손님들 중에는 전쟁에 대해 무지한 군 장교, 배에 대해 아무것도 모르는 해군 장교, 통치 방법을 전혀 모르는 공무원, 그리고 탐욕스러운 눈과 방탕한 도덕성을 가진 위선적인 사제들이 포함되어 있었다.

raw: Projectors who had discovered every kind of remedy for the little evils with which the State was touched, except the remedy of setting to work in earnest to root out a single sin, poured their distracting babble into any ears they could lay hold of, at the reception of Monseigneur.
en: All of them were completely unfit for their jobs, but because they were related to Monseigneur's class, they were given public positions purely for profit. There were dozens of them.
ko: 그들 모두는 직무에 완전히 부적합했지만, 몽세뇌르의 계급과 친척이라는 이유로 오로지 이익을 위해 공직을 얻었다. 그런 사람들이 수십 명이나 되었다.

raw: Unbelieving Philosophers who were remodelling the world with words, and making card-towers of Babel to scale the skies with, talked with Unbelieving Chemists who had an eye on the transmutation of metals, at this wonderful gathering accumulated by Monseigneur.
en: There were also doctors making fortunes by prescribing expensive remedies for imaginary illnesses, smiling at their wealthy patients in the waiting rooms.
ko: 상상 속의 질병에 비싼 치료제를 처방해 큰돈을 벌면서 대기실에 있는 부유한 환자들에게 미소 짓는 의사들도 있었다.

raw: Exquisite gentlemen of the finest breeding, which was at that remarkable time--and has been since--to be known by its fruits of indifference to every natural subject of human interest, were in the most exemplary state of exhaustion, at the hotel of Monseigneur.
en: Elegant gentlemen of the highest social class—who showed their fine breeding back then, and ever since, by not caring about anything that naturally interests normal human beings—were hanging around Monseigneur's hotel in a perfect state of exhaustion.
ko: 일반적인 인간들이 자연스럽게 흥미를 가지는 것에는 전혀 무관심함으로써 그 당시부터 지금까지 자신들의 훌륭한 혈통을 과시해 온 최고 상류층의 우아한 신사들이 완전히 지친 상태로 몽세뇌르의 저택 주변을 어슬렁거리고 있었다.

raw: Such homes had these various notabilities left behind them in the fine world of Paris, that the spies among the assembled devotees of Monseigneur--forming a goodly half of the polite company--would have found it hard to discover among the angels of that sphere one solitary wife, who, in her manners and appearance, owned to being a Mother.
en: Non-believing philosophers talked of remodeling the world with words, while chemists talked of turning lead into gold. Exquisite gentlemen showed their high breeding by acting completely bored by everything.
ko: 불신주의 철학자들은 말로 세상을 재건하는 것에 대해 떠들었고, 화학자들은 납을 금으로 바꾸는 것에 대해 이야기했다. 까다로운 신사들은 모든 것에 완전히 지루해하는 척함으로써 그들의 높은 혈통을 과시했다.

raw: Indeed, except for the mere act of bringing a troublesome creature into this world--which does not go far towards the realisation of the name of mother--there was no such thing known to the fashion.
en: The spies among the guests, who made up at least half the crowd, would have struggled to find a single wife who acted like a real mother to her children.
ko: 군중의 적어도 절반을 차지하는 손님들 중의 스파이들이 자녀들에게 진짜 어머니처럼 행동하는 아내를 단 한 명이라도 찾으려 했다면 고생했을 것이다.

raw: Peasant women kept the unfashionable babies close, and brought them up, and charming grandmammas of sixty dressed and supped as at twenty.
en: In high society, children were sent away to be raised by peasant women, while grandmothers of sixty dressed and dined like young women of twenty.
ko: 상류 사회에서 아이들은 농부 여성들에게 길러지도록 멀리 보내졌고, 반면 60세의 할머니들은 20세의 젊은 여성들처럼 차려입고 식사를 했다.

raw: The leprosy of unreality disfigured every human creature in attendance upon Monseigneur.
en: A sense of unreality clung to everyone around Monseigneur.
ko: 비현실감은 몽세뇌르 주변의 모든 사람에게 달라붙어 있었다.

raw: In the outermost room were half a dozen exceptional people who had had, for a few years, some vague misgiving in them that things in general were going rather wrong.
en: In the outermost room stood a few people who had begun to worry that things in France were going wrong.
ko: 가장 바깥쪽 방에는 프랑스의 사정이 잘못되어 가고 있다고 걱정하기 시작한 소수의 사람들이 서 있었다.

raw: As a promising way of setting them right, half of the half-dozen had become members of a fantastic sect of Convulsionists, and were even then considering within themselves whether they should foam, rage, roar, and turn cataleptic on the spot--thereby setting up a highly intelligible finger-post to the Future, for Monseigneur’s guidance.
en: To find a promising cure for this exhaustion, three of these six gentlemen had joined a wild religious group called the Convulsionists. They were currently wondering if they should start foaming at the mouth, raging, roaring, and freezing in trances right then and there, hoping to provide a very clear sign pointing out the future for Monseigneur's guidance.
ko: 이 피로에 대한 유망한 치료법을 찾기 위해 이 여섯 명의 신사 중 세 명은 경련파라는 거친 종교 단체에 가입했다. 그들은 몽세뇌르의 지도를 위해 미래를 가리키는 매우 명확한 신호를 제공하기를 바라며, 그 자리에서 당장 입에 거품을 물고 분노하고 포효하며 무아지경에 빠져 얼어붙어야 할지 생각하고 있었다.

raw: Besides these Dervishes, were other three who had rushed into another sect, which mended matters with a jargon about “the Centre of Truth:” holding that Man had got out of the Centre of Truth--which did not need much demonstration--but had not got out of the Circumference, and that he was to be kept from flying out of the Circumference, and was even to be shoved back into the Centre, by fasting and seeing of spirits. Among these, accordingly, much discoursing with spirits went on--and it did a world of good which never became manifest.
en: Besides these wild members, the other three gentlemen had rushed to join a different group that tried to fix things with confusing talk about "the Center of Truth." They believed that humanity had wandered away from the Center of Truth—which was pretty obvious—but hadn't quite fallen outside the outer edge yet. Their goal was to keep people from flying off the edge entirely and to shove them back into the Center by fasting and seeing ghosts. Because of this, they spent a lot of time talking to spirits, which supposedly did a world of good, even though no one ever actually saw any positive results from it.
ko: 이 거친 회원들 외에 다른 세 명의 신사는 '진리의 중심'에 대한 혼란스러운 말로 상황을 바로잡으려는 다른 단체에 서둘러 합류했다. 그들은 인류가 진리의 중심에서 멀어졌다고 믿었는데—이는 꽤 명백했다—하지만 아직 바깥쪽 가장자리 밖으로 완전히 떨어지지는 않았다고 보았다. 그들의 목표는 사람들이 가장자리에서 완전히 날아가 버리는 것을 막고, 금식과 유령을 봄으로써 그들을 다시 중심부로 밀어넣는 것이었다. 이 때문에 그들은 정령들과 대화하는 데 많은 시간을 보냈고, 비록 아무도 그것에서 어떤 긍정적인 결과를 실제로 보지 못했지만, 그것이 엄청나게 좋은 일을 한다고 여겨졌다.

raw: But, the comfort was, that all the company at the grand hotel of Monseigneur were perfectly dressed.
en: However, the one comforting thought was that everyone staying at Monseigneur's grand hotel was dressed perfectly.
ko: 그러나 한 가지 위안이 되는 생각은 몽세뇌르의 성대한 저택에 머물고 있는 모든 사람이 완벽하게 차려입었다는 것이었다.

raw: If the Day of Judgment had only been ascertained to be a dress day, everybody there would have been eternally correct.
en: If the Day of Judgment were a fashion show, everyone there would have been saved.
ko: 만약 심판의 날이 패션쇼였다면, 그곳에 있는 모든 사람은 구원을 받았을 것이다.

raw: Such frizzling and powdering and sticking up of hair, such delicate complexions artificially preserved and mended, such gallant swords to look at, and such delicate honour to the sense of smell, would surely keep anything going, for ever and ever.
en: They had powdered hair, painted faces, fine swords, and expensive perfumes. They looked capable of keeping the system going forever.
ko: 그들은 분칠을 한 머리, 화장한 얼굴, 훌륭한 칼, 그리고 비싼 향수를 가졌다. 그들은 이 체제를 영원히 지속시킬 수 있을 것처럼 보였다.

raw: The exquisite gentlemen of the finest breeding wore little pendent trinkets that chinked as they languidly moved; these golden fetters rang like precious little bells; and what with that ringing, and with the rustle of silk and brocade and fine linen, there was a flutter in the air that fanned Saint Antoine and his devouring hunger far away.
en: The gentlemen wore gold trinkets that jingled as they walked like little bells. Between the jingling and the rustling of silk and fine linen, the air was filled with a flurry that blew the memory of the starving people of Saint Antoine far away.
ko: 신사들은 걸을 때마다 작은 방울처럼 딸랑거리는 금 장신구를 달고 있었다. 딸랑거리는 소리와 실크와 고운 리넨이 스치는 소리 사이로, 생탕투안의 굶주린 사람들에 대한 기억을 저 멀리 날려버리는 작은 돌풍이 공기를 채웠다.

raw: Dress was the one unfailing talisman and charm used for keeping all things in their places.
en: Fashionable dress was the magic charm used to keep everything in its place.
ko: 유행하는 옷은 모든 것을 제자리에 유지하는 데 사용되는 마법의 주문이었다.

raw: Everybody was dressed for a Fancy Ball that was never to leave off.
en: Everyone acted as if they were at a never-ending costume ball.
ko: 모든 사람이 마치 끝없는 가장무도회에 있는 것처럼 행동했다.

raw: From the Palace of the Tuileries, through Monseigneur and the whole Court, through the Chambers, the Tribunals of Justice, and all society (except the scarecrows), the Fancy Ball descended to the Common Executioner: who, in pursuance of the charm, was required to officiate “frizzled, powdered, in a gold-laced coat, pumps, and white silk stockings.” At the gallows and the wheel--the axe was a rarity--Monsieur Paris, as it was the episcopal mode among his brother Professors of the provinces, Monsieur Orleans, and the rest, to call him, presided in this dainty dress.
en: This obsession with dressing up like it was a costume party trickled all the way down from the royal Palace of the Tuileries, past Monseigneur and the entire Court, through the government chambers, the courts of justice, and all of high society (ignoring the poor people in rags), until it reached the common executioner. To keep the glamorous illusion going, the executioner had to do his grim job with curled and powdered hair, wearing a gold-laced coat, dress shoes, and white silk stockings. At the gallows and the breaking wheel—the executioner's axe was rarely used—Monsieur Paris, which is what his fellow executioners from the provinces like Monsieur Orleans respectfully called him, presided over the executions in this delicate and fancy outfit.
ko: 마치 가장무도회인 것처럼 차려입는 것에 대한 이 집착은 왕궁인 튈르리 궁전에서부터 시작되어, 몽세뇌르와 궁정 전체를 지나, 정부 기관들, 사법 재판소들, 그리고 상류 사회 전체(누더기를 입은 가난한 사람들은 무시한 채)로 흘러내려 와, 마침내 흔한 사형 집행인에게까지 이르렀다. 그 화려한 환상을 유지하기 위해 사형 집행인은 구부러지고 분칠된 머리에 금색 끈이 달린 코트, 정장 구두, 그리고 하얀 실크 스타킹을 신고 그의 끔찍한 직무를 수행해야 했다. 교수대와 수레바퀴 처형대에서—사형 집행인의 도끼는 거의 사용되지 않았다—지방에서 온 오를레앙 씨와 같은 그의 동료 사형 집행인들이 정중하게 파리 씨라고 불렀던 그는, 이 섬세하고 화려한 복장으로 처형을 주재했다.

raw: And who among the company at Monseigneur’s reception in that seventeen hundred and eightieth year of our Lord, could possibly doubt, that a system rooted in a frizzled hangman, powdered, gold-laced, pumped, and white-silk stockinged, would see the very stars out!
en: And who among the guests at Monseigneur's reception in the year 1780 could possibly doubt that a whole social system based around a hangman with curled hair, powdered, dressed in gold lace, dress shoes, and white silk stockings would last forever, even outliving the stars themselves!
ko: 그리고 1780년 몽세뇌르의 연회에 참석한 손님들 중 누가, 구부러진 머리에 분칠을 하고 금색 끈을 달고 정장 구두와 하얀 실크 스타킹을 신은 사형 집행인을 기반으로 한 전체 사회 체제가 영원히, 심지어 별들보다 더 오래 지속될 것이라는 점을 의심할 수 있었겠는가!

raw: Monseigneur having eased his four men of their burdens and taken his chocolate, caused the doors of the Holiest of Holiests to be thrown open, and issued forth.
en: After Monseigneur had relieved his four servants of their duties and finished drinking his chocolate, he had the doors to his private inner room thrown wide open and finally came out.
ko: 몽세뇌르는 네 명의 하인들의 임무를 면제해주고 초콜릿을 다 마신 후, 자신의 개인 내실 문을 활짝 열게 하고 마침내 밖으로 나왔다.

raw: Then, what submission, what cringing and fawning, what servility, what abject humiliation!
en: The crowd bowed, flattered, and humbled themselves before him.
ko: 군중은 고개를 숙이고, 아첨하며, 그 앞에서 자신들을 낮추었다.

raw: As to bowing down in body and spirit, nothing in that way was left for Heaven--which may have been one among other reasons why the worshippers of Monseigneur never troubled it.
en: They showed so much devotion that they left nothing for God, which was probably why they never bothered to pray.
ko: 그들은 하나님을 위해서는 아무것도 남기지 않을 만큼 너무 많은 헌신을 보여주었고, 그것이 아마도 그들이 굳이 기도하지 않았던 이유일 것이다.

raw: Bestowing a word of promise here and a smile there, a whisper on one happy slave and a wave of the hand on another, Monseigneur affably passed through his rooms to the remote region of the Circumference of Truth.
en: Giving a promise here and a smile there, whispering to one happy guest and waving to another, Monseigneur walked through the rooms.
ko: 여기서 약속을 하고 저기서 미소를 지으며, 한 행복한 손님에게 속삭이고 다른 손님에게 손을 흔들면서 몽세뇌르는 방을 걸어갔다.

raw: There, Monseigneur turned, and came back again, and so in due course of time got himself shut up in his sanctuary by the chocolate sprites, and was seen no more.
en: He then turned and returned to his private room, shut in once more by his servants, and was seen no more.
ko: 그러고 나서 그는 몸을 돌려 개인 방으로 돌아갔고, 그의 하인들에 의해 다시 한번 문이 닫혔으며 더 이상 보이지 않았다.

raw: The show being over, the flutter in the air became quite a little storm, and the precious little bells went ringing downstairs.
en: With the reception over, the guests hurried downstairs, their gold trinkets jingling.
ko: 연회가 끝나자 손님들은 금 장신구를 딸랑거리며 서둘러 아래층으로 내려갔다.

raw: There was soon but one person left of all the crowd, and he, with his hat under his arm and his snuff-box in his hand, slowly passed among the mirrors on his way out.
en: Soon only one man was left, slowly walking past the mirrors on his way out, holding his hat and snuffbox.
ko: 곧 단 한 남자만이 남아 모자와 코담뱃갑을 든 채 밖으로 나가는 길에 거울들을 지나 천천히 걸어가고 있었다.

raw: “I devote you,” said this person, stopping at the last door on his way, and turning in the direction of the sanctuary, “to the Devil!”
en: "I condemn you," he muttered, stopping at the door and looking back toward Monseigneur's room, "to the Devil!"
ko: "나는 너를 저주한다," 문에 멈춰 서서 몽세뇌르의 방 쪽을 뒤돌아보며 그가 중얼거렸다. "악마에게나 가버려라!"

raw: With that, he shook the snuff from his fingers as if he had shaken the dust from his feet, and quietly walked downstairs.
en: He shook the snuff from his fingers as if shaking dust from his shoes, and walked downstairs.
ko: 그는 신발에서 먼지를 털어내듯 손가락에서 코담배를 털어내고 아래층으로 걸어 내려갔다.

raw: He was a man of about sixty, handsomely dressed, haughty in manner, and with a face like a fine mask.
en: He was a man of about sixty, handsomely dressed, proud, with a face like a mask.
ko: 그는 60세가량의 단정하게 차려입은 자부심이 강한 남자로, 가면 같은 얼굴을 하고 있었다.

raw: A face of a transparent paleness; every feature in it clearly defined; one set expression on it.
en: His face was very pale, with sharp features and a cold expression.
ko: 그의 얼굴은 창백했고, 날카로운 이목구비에 차가운 표정을 짓고 있었다.

raw: The nose, beautifully formed otherwise, was very slightly pinched at the top of each nostril.
en: His nose was well-shaped, but pinched at the nostrils.
ko: 그의 코는 모양이 잘 잡혀 있었지만, 콧구멍이 좁아져 있었다.

raw: In those two compressions, or dints, the only little change that the face ever showed, resided. They persisted in changing colour sometimes, and they would be occasionally dilated and contracted by something like a faint pulsation; then, they gave a look of treachery, and cruelty, to the whole countenance.
en: This pinching was the only part of his face that ever changed, turning white or twitching slightly when he was angry, giving him a look of cruelty and treachery.
ko: 이 좁아진 부분은 그의 얼굴에서 유일하게 변하는 부분이었는데, 그가 화가 났을 때 하얗게 변하거나 약간 씰룩거리면서 그에게 잔인함과 배반의 인상을 주었다.

raw: Examined with attention, its capacity of helping such a look was to be found in the line of the mouth, and the lines of the orbits of the eyes, being much too horizontal and thin; still, in the effect of the face made, it was a handsome face, and a remarkable one.
en: If you looked closely, you could see that this cruel expression came from the line of his mouth and the shape of his eye sockets, which were far too thin and straight. But despite all that, it was still a very handsome and striking face.
ko: 자세히 보면 이 잔인한 표정은 너무 얇고 일직선인 입매와 눈구멍 모양에서 비롯된 것임을 알 수 있었다. 하지만 그 모든 것에도 불구하고 그것은 여전히 매우 잘생기고 눈에 띄는 얼굴이었다.

raw: Its owner went downstairs into the courtyard, got into his carriage, and drove away.
en: He went down to the courtyard, got into his carriage, and drove away.
ko: 그는 마당으로 내려가 마차에 올라타고는 가버렸다.

raw: Not many people had talked with him at the reception; he had stood in a little space apart, and Monseigneur might have been warmer in his manner.
en: Few people had spoken to him at the reception, and Monseigneur had been cold to him.
ko: 리셉션에서 그에게 말을 건넨 사람은 거의 없었고, 몽세뇌르도 그에게 냉담했다.

raw: It appeared, under the circumstances, rather agreeable to him to see the common people dispersed before his horses, and often barely escaping from being run down.
en: Under the circumstances, he seemed to enjoy seeing the common people scatter before his horses, barely escaping with their lives.
ko: 이러한 상황에서 그는 평민들이 그의 말 앞에서 가까스로 목숨을 건지며 흩어지는 것을 즐기는 듯했다.

raw: His man drove as if he were charging an enemy, and the furious recklessness of the man brought no check into the face, or to the lips, of the master.
en: His driver drove recklessly, as if charging into battle, and the master did not stop him.
ko: 마부는 마치 전투에 돌진하듯 난폭하게 마차를 몰았지만, 주인은 그를 말리지 않았다.

raw: The complaint had sometimes made itself audible, even in that deaf city and dumb age, that, in the narrow streets without footways, the fierce patrician custom of hard driving endangered and maimed the mere vulgar in a barbarous manner.
en: Even in that deaf city and ignorant age, people had sometimes managed to voice their complaints that the rich nobles' aggressive habit of driving their carriages recklessly fast through the narrow, sidewalk-less streets was violently injuring and killing common people in a brutal way.
ko: 그 귀먹은 도시와 무지한 시대에도, 사람들은 때때로 인도도 없는 좁은 거리를 난폭하고 빠르게 마차를 모는 부유한 귀족들의 공격적인 습관이 평민들을 잔인하게 다치게 하고 죽인다고 불만을 표출하곤 했다.

raw: But, few cared enough for that to think of it a second time, and, in this matter, as in all others, the common wretches were left to get out of their difficulties as they could.
en: But few wealthy people cared, and the poor were left to get out of the way as best they could.
ko: 하지만 신경 쓰는 부자는 거의 없었고, 가난한 사람들은 알아서 길을 비켜야만 했다.

raw: With a wild rattle and clatter, and an inhuman abandonment of consideration not easy to be understood in these days, the carriage dashed through streets and swept round corners, with women screaming before it, and men clutching each other and clutching children out of its way.
en: With a loud clatter and a complete lack of concern, the carriage sped through the streets and around corners. Women screamed, and men grabbed their children to pull them out of the way.
ko: 요란한 소리를 내며 전혀 아랑곳하지 않고 마차는 거리를 달리고 모퉁이를 돌았다. 여자들은 비명을 질렀고, 남자들은 아이들을 붙잡아 길 밖으로 끌어냈다.

raw: At last, swooping at a street corner by a fountain, one of its wheels came to a sickening little jolt, and there was a loud cry from a number of voices, and the horses reared and plunged.
en: Suddenly, near a fountain at a street corner, a wheel hit something with a sickening jolt. The horses reared, and the crowd screamed.
ko: 갑자기 어느 길모퉁이의 분수 근처에서 바퀴가 역겨운 충격과 함께 무언가에 부딪혔다. 말들은 뒷다리로 섰고, 군중은 비명을 질렀다.

raw: But for the latter inconvenience, the carriage probably would not have stopped; carriages were often known to drive on, and leave their wounded behind, and why not?
en: If the horses hadn't stopped, the carriage would have driven on, leaving the injured behind.
ko: 말들이 멈추지 않았다면 마차는 부상자를 남겨둔 채 계속 달렸을 것이다.

raw: But the frightened valet had got down in a hurry, and there were twenty hands at the horses’ bridles.
en: But the driver quickly got down, and several people grabbed the horses' reins.
ko: 하지만 마부는 재빨리 내려왔고, 몇몇 사람들이 말의 고삐를 붙잡았다.

raw: “What has gone wrong?” said Monsieur, calmly looking out.
en: "What is the matter?" the master asked, looking out calmly.
ko: "무슨 일이냐?" 주인이 차분하게 밖을 내다보며 물었다.

raw: A tall man in a nightcap had caught up a bundle from among the feet of the horses, and had laid it on the basement of the fountain, and was down in the mud and wet, howling over it like a wild animal.
en: A tall man in a nightcap had picked up a bundle from under the horses' hooves and laid it by the fountain. He was kneeling in the mud, crying out like a wild animal.
ko: 나이트캡을 쓴 키 큰 남자가 말발굽 아래에서 무언가 꾸러미를 집어 들어 분수대 옆에 눕혔다. 그는 진흙 속에 무릎을 꿇고 야생동물처럼 울부짖고 있었다.

raw: “Pardon, Monsieur the Marquis!” said a ragged and submissive man, “it is a child.”
en: "Pardon, Monsieur the Marquis!" said a poor man, bowing. "It is a child."
ko: "죄송합니다, 후작님!" 가난한 남자가 허리를 굽히며 말했다. "아이입니다."

raw: “Why does he make that abominable noise?
en: "Why is he making that terrible noise?
ko: "저 자는 왜 저런 끔찍한 소리를 내는 거냐?

raw: Is it his child?”
en: Is it his child?"
ko: 그의 아이냐?"

raw: “Excuse me, Monsieur the Marquis--it is a pity--yes.”
en: "Excuse me, Monsieur the Marquis, yes, unfortunately."
ko: "죄송합니다만, 후작님, 불행히도 그렇습니다."

raw: The fountain was a little removed; for the street opened, where it was, into a space some ten or twelve yards square.
en: The fountain was set back a little bit from the main road, because right where it stood, the street opened up into a small square area about ten or twelve yards wide.
ko: 분수대는 길에서 약간 뒤로 물러나 있었는데, 그곳에 약 10~12야드 너비의 작은 광장 같은 공간이 펼쳐져 있었기 때문이다.

raw: As the tall man suddenly got up from the ground, and came running at the carriage, Monsieur the Marquis clapped his hand for an instant on his sword-hilt.
en: As the tall man suddenly stood up and ran toward the carriage, the Marquis put his hand on his sword.
ko: 키 큰 남자가 갑자기 일어나 마차를 향해 달려오자, 후작은 칼에 손을 얹었다.

raw: “Killed!” shrieked the man, in wild desperation, extending both arms at their length above his head, and staring at him. “Dead!”
en: "Killed!" the man shrieked in wild desperation, stretching both of his arms straight up high above his head and staring right at him. "Dead!"
ko: "죽었어!" 그 남자는 두 팔을 머리 위로 높이 뻗고 그를 똑바로 쳐다보며 미친 듯한 절망 속에서 비명을 질렀다. "죽었다고!"

raw: The people closed round, and looked at Monsieur the Marquis.
en: The crowd gathered around and looked at the Marquis.
ko: 군중이 모여들어 후작을 바라보았다.

raw: There was nothing revealed by the many eyes that looked at him but watchfulness and eagerness; there was no visible menacing or anger.
en: The many eyes staring at him didn't show any visible threats or anger at all; they only revealed a quiet watchfulness and an eager curiosity.
ko: 그를 응시하는 많은 눈빛은 어떠한 눈에 띄는 위협이나 분노도 전혀 보여주지 않았다. 단지 조용한 경계와 강렬한 호기심만을 드러낼 뿐이었다.

raw: Neither did the people say anything; after the first cry, they had been silent, and they remained so.
en: The people didn't say a single word either; after their very first cry, they had gone completely silent, and they stayed that way.
ko: 사람들은 단 한마디도 하지 않았다. 첫 번째 비명을 지른 후 그들은 완전히 침묵했고, 계속 그 상태로 머물렀다.

raw: The voice of the submissive man who had spoken, was flat and tame in its extreme submission.
en: The man who had spoken sounded humble and frightened.
ko: 말을 했던 남자의 목소리는 겸손하고 겁에 질려 있었다.

raw: Monsieur the Marquis ran his eyes over them all, as if they had been mere rats come out of their holes.
en: The Marquis looked at them as if they were rats coming out of their holes.
ko: 후작은 쥐들이 쥐구멍에서 기어나온 것처럼 그들을 쳐다보았다.

raw: He took out his purse.
en: He took out his purse.
ko: 그는 지갑을 꺼냈다.

raw: “It is extraordinary to me,” said he, “that you people cannot take care of yourselves and your children.
en: He said, "It is strange to me that you people cannot take care of yourselves and your children.
ko: 그는 말했다. "너희들이 너희 자신과 아이들을 돌보지 못한다는 게 참 이상하구나.

raw: One or the other of you is for ever in the way.
en: You are always in the way.
ko: 너희는 항상 방해만 돼.

raw: How do I know what injury you have done my horses.
en: For all I know, you have injured my horses.
ko: 어쩌면 너희 때문에 내 말들이 다쳤을지도 모르지.

raw: See!
en: Here!
ko: 자!

raw: Give him that.”
en: Give him this."
ko: 이걸 그에게 주어라."

raw: He threw out a gold coin for the valet to pick up, and all the heads craned forward that all the eyes might look down at it as it fell.
en: He threw a gold coin out for the driver to pick up, and the crowd stared at it as it fell.
ko: 그는 마부가 주울 수 있도록 금화 하나를 던졌고, 군중은 그것이 떨어지는 것을 지켜보았다.

raw: The tall man called out again with a most unearthly cry, “Dead!”
en: The tall man cried out again, "Dead!"
ko: 키 큰 남자가 다시 울부짖었다. "죽었어!"

raw: He was arrested by the quick arrival of another man, for whom the rest made way.
en: He was stopped by the arrival of another man, for whom the crowd made way.
ko: 군중이 길을 터주며 다른 남자가 도착하자 그는 멈칫했다.

raw: On seeing him, the miserable creature fell upon his shoulder, sobbing and crying, and pointing to the fountain, where some women were stooping over the motionless bundle, and moving gently about it.
en: Seeing him, the father fell on his shoulder, sobbing and pointing to the fountain where some women were looking at the still bundle.
ko: 그를 보자, 아이의 아버지는 그의 어깨에 기대어 흐느끼며, 몇몇 여자들이 움직이지 않는 꾸러미를 바라보고 있는 분수대를 가리켰다.

raw: They were as silent, however, as the men.
en: The women were as quiet as the men.
ko: 여자들도 남자들만큼이나 조용했다.

raw: “I know all, I know all,” said the last comer. “Be a brave man, my Gaspard!
en: "I know, I know," said the newcomer. "Be brave, Gaspard.
ko: "알아, 안다고," 새로 온 사람이 말했다. "용기를 내, 가스파르.

raw: It is better for the poor little plaything to die so, than to live.
en: It is better for the poor child to die like this than to live in misery.
ko: 가엾은 아이가 비참하게 사는 것보다 이렇게 죽는 편이 나아.

raw: It has died in a moment without pain.
en: It died in a moment, without pain.
ko: 고통 없이 한순간에 죽었잖아.

raw: Could it have lived an hour as happily?”
en: Could it have lived a happy life?"
ko: 행복한 삶을 살 수 있었겠어?"

raw: “You are a philosopher, you there,” said the Marquis, smiling. “How do they call you?”
en: "You are a philosopher," the Marquis said, smiling. "What is your name?"
ko: "철학자 시로군," 후작이 미소를 지으며 말했다. "이름이 뭔가?"

raw: “They call me Defarge.”
en: "They call me Defarge."
ko: "사람들은 저를 드파르지라고 부릅니다."

raw: “Of what trade?”
en: "What is your trade?"
ko: "직업이 뭔가?"

raw: “Monsieur the Marquis, vendor of wine.”
en: "I sell wine, Monsieur the Marquis."
ko: "와인을 팝니다, 후작님."

raw: “Pick up that, philosopher and vendor of wine,” said the Marquis, throwing him another gold coin, “and spend it as you will.
en: "Pick that up, philosopher and wine seller," said the Marquis, throwing him another gold coin. "Spend it as you like.
ko: "주워라, 철학자이자 와인 상인," 후작이 또 다른 금화를 던지며 말했다. "마음대로 써라.

raw: The horses there; are they right?”
en: Are the horses ready?"
ko: 말들은 준비되었나?"

raw: Without deigning to look at the assemblage a second time, Monsieur the Marquis leaned back in his seat, and was just being driven away with the air of a gentleman who had accidentally broke some common thing, and had paid for it, and could afford to pay for it; when his ease was suddenly disturbed by a coin flying into his carriage, and ringing on its floor.
en: Without looking at the crowd again, the Marquis leaned back, preparing to drive away like a gentleman who had broken a cheap object and paid for it. Suddenly, a coin was thrown back into the carriage, ringing on the floor.
ko: 후작은 군중을 다시 보지도 않고 등받이에 기댔다. 마치 싸구려 물건을 부수고 값을 지불한 신사처럼 마차를 출발시킬 준비를 했다. 그 순간, 금화 하나가 마차 안으로 다시 날아와 바닥에 떨어지며 쨍그랑 소리를 냈다.

raw: “Hold!” said Monsieur the Marquis. “Hold the horses!
en: "Stop!" the Marquis called out. "Hold the horses!
ko: "멈춰라!" 후작이 소리쳤다. "말들을 잡아!

raw: Who threw that?”
en: Who threw that?"
ko: 누가 던졌지?"

raw: He looked to the spot where Defarge the vendor of wine had stood, a moment before; but the wretched father was grovelling on his face on the pavement in that spot, and the figure that stood beside him was the figure of a dark stout woman, knitting.
en: He looked toward where Defarge had been standing. The father was on the pavement, crying. Next to him stood a stout, dark woman, knitting.
ko: 그는 드파르지가 서 있던 곳을 향해 시선을 돌렸다. 아버지는 보도에 엎드려 울고 있었다. 그 옆에는 뚱뚱하고 어두운 인상의 여자가 뜨개질을 하며 서 있었다.

raw: “You dogs!” said the Marquis, but smoothly, and with an unchanged front, except as to the spots on his nose: “I would ride over any of you very willingly, and exterminate you from the earth.
en: "You dogs!" the Marquis said calmly, his nostrils twitching. "I would gladly run over all of you and wipe you off the earth.
ko: "이 개 같은 것들!" 후작은 차분하게 말했지만 그의 콧방울이 씰룩거렸다. "기꺼이 너희 모두를 밟고 지나가서 이 땅에서 쓸어버리겠다.

raw: If I knew which rascal threw at the carriage, and if that brigand were sufficiently near it, he should be crushed under the wheels.”
en: If I knew who threw that coin, I would crush him under the wheels."
ko: 누가 그 동전을 던졌는지 안다면 바퀴 밑에 깔아 뭉개버렸을 것이다."

raw: So cowed was their condition, and so long and hard their experience of what such a man could do to them, within the law and beyond it, that not a voice, or a hand, or even an eye was raised.
en: The crowd was so cowed and used to his power that no one raised a hand or said a word.
ko: 군중은 너무나 겁에 질려 있었고 그의 권력에 익숙해져 있어서 아무도 손을 들거나 말 한마디 하지 못했다.

raw: Among the men, not one. But the woman who stood knitting looked up steadily, and looked the Marquis in the face.
en: But the woman who stood knitting looked the Marquis straight in the eye.
ko: 하지만 뜨개질을 하며 서 있던 여자는 후작의 눈을 똑바로 쳐다보았다.

raw: It was not for his dignity to notice it; his contemptuous eyes passed over her, and over all the other rats; and he leaned back in his seat again, and gave the word “Go on!”
en: It was beneath his dignity to pay attention to it; his scornful eyes just swept right past her, and over all the rest of the people as if they were rats. Then he leaned back in his seat again and gave the order, "Go on!"
ko: 그것에 신경 쓰는 것은 그의 품위에 맞지 않았다. 그의 경멸적인 시선은 단지 그녀를 스쳐 지나갔고, 나머지 모든 사람들을 마치 쥐를 보듯 훑어보았다. 그리고 그는 다시 좌석에 기대앉아 명령했다. "출발해!"

raw: He was driven on, and other carriages came whirling by in quick succession; the Minister, the State-Projector, the Farmer-General, the Doctor, the Lawyer, the Ecclesiastic, the Grand Opera, the Comedy, the whole Fancy Ball in a bright continuous flow, came whirling by.
en: He drove away. Other carriages followed in quick succession, the ministers, tax collectors, doctors, and lawyers. They were all part of the grand costume ball.
ko: 그는 마차를 몰고 떠났다. 다른 마차들이 그 뒤를 빠르게 따랐는데, 장관, 세금 징수원, 의사, 변호사들이었다. 그들은 모두 거대한 가장무도회의 일부였다.

raw: The rats had crept out of their holes to look on, and they remained looking on for hours; soldiers and police often passing between them and the spectacle, and making a barrier behind which they slunk, and through which they peeped.
en: The poor people, like rats creeping out of their holes, had come out to watch, and they stayed there looking on for hours. Soldiers and police officers often marched between the crowd and the scene, forming a barrier that the people slinked behind and tried to peek through.
ko: 가난한 사람들은 마치 구멍에서 기어 나오는 쥐들처럼 구경하러 나왔고, 몇 시간 동안 그곳에 머물며 지켜보았다. 군인들과 경찰들이 종종 군중과 현장 사이를 행진하며 장벽을 형성했고, 사람들은 그 뒤로 몰래 숨어 틈새로 엿보려 했다.

raw: The father had long ago taken up his bundle and bidden himself away with it, when the women who had tended the bundle while it lay on the base of the fountain, sat there watching the running of the water and the rolling of the Fancy Ball--when the one woman who had stood conspicuous, knitting, still knitted on with the steadfastness of Fate.
en: The father had carried his dead child away. The women sat by the fountain, watching the water flow and the carriages pass, while the woman who had stood knitting continued to knit like the figure of Fate.
ko: 아버지는 죽은 아이를 안고 가버렸다. 여자들은 분수대 곁에 앉아 물이 흐르는 것과 마차들이 지나가는 것을 바라보았고, 한편 서서 뜨개질을 하던 여자는 운명의 여신처럼 계속 뜨개질을 했다.

raw: The water of the fountain ran, the swift river ran, the day ran into evening, so much life in the city ran into death according to rule, time and tide waited for no man, the rats were sleeping close together in their dark holes again, the Fancy Ball was lighted up at supper, all things ran their course.
en: The water ran, the river flowed, day turned to evening, and life in the city turned to death. The poor went back to their dark rooms, the rich lit up their dinners, and everything continued as before.
ko: 물은 흐르고, 강물도 흘러, 낮은 저녁이 되었고, 도시의 삶은 죽음으로 변했다. 가난한 사람들은 어두운 방으로 돌아갔고, 부자들은 저녁 만찬을 밝혔으며, 모든 것은 이전처럼 계속되었다.
